name: Vitaphone synchronized sound cinema
description: A commercial cinema system synchronized film projection with a recorded sound disc, enabling a recorded musical accompaniment.

date.label: 6 August 1926
date.basis: Date or stated historical interval in cited source; see caveats.

events.statement: Warner Bros. presented Don Juan with a synchronized recorded musical soundtrack.

evidence.supports: Filmography dates the synchronized music Don Juan exhibition to 6 August 1926.

events.caveats: Feature used synchronized music and effects; the system was not the first attempt at film sound.

events.statement: The Jazz Singer was shown in New York with synchronized songs and some spoken dialogue.
events.caveats: Some markets received a silent version; equipped theatres were needed for the synchronized soundtrack.

earliest_record.rationale: Earliest dated witness established by the cited source for this scoped record, not a claim of global first.

caveats: Other synchronized film-sound processes and shorts predated Vitaphone; this record tracks a commercial system and its documented exhibitions.

research.note: Initial sourced research; independent review pending. Independent reader checked dates and sound-on-disc scope in the Museum of the Moving Image and Library of Congress essay; the earlier filmography PDF URL was inaccessible during review.
